beats.text: Why are bridges full of triangles?
Push on a square, and it folds flat.
Push on a triangle, and nothing happens.
A triangle can't change its shape, unless a side changes length.
So when a truck rolls across, the load flows through the triangles.
Some beams get squeezed. Others get stretched.
Ideally, none of them bend, and steel is far stronger that way.
Light. Strong. Rigid. That's a truss.
Which machine should we break down next?
